tasks.short: Notify a supervisor about a major equipment repair.

steps.what: Inspect the failed camera, mixer, display or signal path at the production location and note the symptom, safety risk and effect on the run
Create an internal repair notice containing the asset tag, observed symptom, production impact, photos and requested urgency
Notify the supervisor of the observed production impact and agree whether to substitute, isolate or stop using the equipment

tasks.design: The repair form preserves asset and symptom details, but the technician inspects the equipment and speaks to the supervisor about the live production consequence.
tasks.previous_blocker: Critical repair notices lose asset, symptom or impact details when they are relayed verbally.
tasks.enabler_now: An internal equipment register can prefill the asset and retain incident photos.
tasks.still_hard: Whether a fault is unsafe or can be worked around depends on the physical setup and production context.
tasks.human_edge: The technician can see the failure and explain its practical impact to the supervisor.

ambition.what: Review repeated failures by asset type and production impact.

tasks.altitude: The technician improves equipment readiness by turning observed faults into complete repair records.

evidence.claim: An internal asset register can retain a repair notice with an asset identifier and attached observations.

assumptions: The boundary ends with supervisor notification, not a repair purchase or external vendor instruction.
Asset tags are visible at the production location.
One hour per 100 baseline hours is allowed for maintaining the repair form.
unknowns: Whether technicians can access the asset register from every production location.
research_questions: Which repair notices are currently returned for missing details?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The technician already performs the inspection, notice and supervisor communication; the proposed form improves completeness, not human labour time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Diagnose and resolve a media-system problem.

steps.what: Reproduce the reported picture, sound, playback or routing fault at the affected workstation or venue rack
Trace power, cables, input selection, network link, firmware state and source media to isolate the likely failed component
Replace, reconnect, reconfigure or reset the identified component and test picture, sound and control functions under production conditions
Record the failed component, corrective action and test result in the equipment history

tasks.design: The register can prefill the fault-history record after testing, while the technician performs physical diagnosis and corrective work.
tasks.previous_blocker: Fault history is written up after the repair and is often incomplete.
tasks.enabler_now: A repair form can carry the asset tag, failed component and test result into the equipment history.
tasks.still_hard: Signal faults depend on the specific physical wiring, configuration and source media.
tasks.human_edge: The technician uses observation and hands-on tests to isolate a failure safely.

ambition.what: Use repair history to identify components that should be replaced before failure.

tasks.altitude: The technician builds reliable media systems through better fault evidence and recurring-failure analysis.

evidence.claim: An equipment record can capture a fault, corrective action and test result.

assumptions: The boundary is a repaired and tested system, not a procurement decision.
Technicians retain authority to make reversible configuration and connection changes.
One hour per 100 baseline hours is allowed for history-field maintenance.
unknowns: Which media systems expose useful diagnostic logs.
research_questions: Which failure modes recur after a first repair?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The physical diagnosis and repair remain; automatic history entry improves traceability rather than reducing the core labour.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Direct and coordinate assistants during production.

steps.what: Inspect the venue, running order, crew availability, equipment readiness and current production changes before the call
Assign assistants to camera, audio, lighting, playback or cable tasks and explain the timing, safety constraints and handoffs
Adjust assignments when a cue changes, a person is unavailable or technical work interrupts the production plan

tasks.design: A running-order view can show crew availability and open tasks, but live direction and reprioritisation remain the technician's work.
tasks.previous_blocker: The technician holds the changing crew picture in memory while moving around the venue.
tasks.enabler_now: A shared internal running-order view can make current assignments visible.
tasks.still_hard: Production changes and people need immediate contextual direction.
tasks.human_edge: The technician sees the venue and can give clear, safe priorities.

ambition.what: Review recurring coordination failures after productions.

tasks.altitude: The technician improves production readiness and coaching rather than merely assigning shifts.

evidence.claim: A shared internal view can display a running order and crew assignments.

assumptions: The boundary is the production call and live coordination, not performance evaluation.
The running order remains an aid rather than a substitute for a verbal safety briefing.
One hour per 100 baseline hours is allowed for maintaining the assignment view.
unknowns: Whether assistants have reliable access to the view during venue setup.
research_questions: Which production changes most often require reassignment?

already_counted.description: Venue assessment, direction and live coordination

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Coordination and direction remain human work; the view improves shared awareness but adds upkeep.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Compress, digitise, duplicate and store audio or video data.

steps.what: Inspect source tapes, cards or files, identify the required preservation or delivery format, and label the media with its project and rights context
Ingest the source, create the specified digital master and derivative, calculate checksums and place the copies in the designated storage locations
Play back the converted master and derivative, verify audio, picture, duration, sync and checksum status, and decide whether to reprocess
Record the verified formats, storage locations, checksums and rights label in the media catalogue

tasks.design: The processing service creates specified formats, checksums and storage copies. The technician judges source condition and verifies that the resulting media is usable.
tasks.previous_blocker: The technician watches batch conversion and enters the same storage metadata after each job.
tasks.enabler_now: A processing queue can apply a chosen format preset and retain checksums with each output.
tasks.still_hard: Source condition, requested format and perceptual quality must be assessed against the production need.
tasks.human_edge: The technician can detect sync, picture or audio faults that a checksum cannot reveal.

ambition.what: Use reprocess causes to improve ingest presets and source-handling guidance.

tasks.altitude: The technician protects media quality and preservation decisions while routine transcoding runs automatically.

evidence.claim: A media-processing queue can create configured derivatives and checksum records from supplied source files.

assumptions: The boundary ends with internal storage and catalogue metadata, not publication or delivery to an external party.
The ingest plan specifies the format preset and storage class before processing begins.
A failed checksum or quality review prevents catalogue completion.
Two hours per 100 baseline hours are allowed for format presets and storage monitoring.
unknowns: Which legacy media formats require manual capture equipment.
research_questions: What proportion of conversions fail visual or audio quality review?

incremental.description: Maintain processing presets and storage monitoring

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Configured processing and catalogue entry are automated; source inspection and quality review remain, with preset maintenance deducted.
